text:
Maria: FYI - found a nasty interaction in staging when a user set runtime.flags.safeguard_ttl to 0. Config daemons immediately re-fetched and pushed CPU on config-service to 4x. Can we halt the console rollout until we have mitigations?
Vik: Can you paste the quick repro and the service logs? Is it all clients or a misbehaving client?
Maria: Repro in staging: change via console preview -> publish -> clients get invalidation event and all call /v1/configs/fetch. Logs: ```2026-02-11T09:04:01Z config-service INFO publish change runtime.flags.safeguard_ttl=0 by maria.console
2026-02-11T09:04:01Z edge-proxy WARN client cache miss for key=runtime.flags.safeguard host=svc-web-77
2026-02-11T09:04:02Z config-service WARN fetch qps spike=4200 baseline=900 cpu=84% p95=410ms```
config-bot: Change recorded: https://console.redwood.internal/configs/runtime.flags (id: ch-7a2b). Alert: config_fetch_qps above expected.
Lee: TTL=0 being "always-expire" was the original intent for certain safety checks. We can't silently change the semantic without owner consent.
Sylvie: Short-term we should block any console publish that would set TTL to 0 for production. Longer term we need agreed semantics.
Vik: Short mitigation options: (1) console validation that prevents TTL==0 for prod (with an override pathway), (2) runtime hotpatch to coerce TTL values < 500ms to 500ms for 1 hour after the change, (3) client-side debounce/jitter so invalidation doesn't cause synchronized fetch.
Maria: I propose a preflight estimator in preview that will compute expected refetch load given active_host_count and ttl change. Inputs: change-id, new_ttl, scope. Output: estimated qps, expected latency delta, and a risk level.
Lee: Good. Also add a telemetry tag with change-id to all config_fetch events for 15 minutes so we can correlate. Add a dash widget: change-id, author, estimated qps, observed qps, p95, error-rate.
Vik: Server-side short-term defenses: rate-limit per-auth-token / per-ip and a short "return-stale-for" header (1-2s) so clients can stagger fetches. Those are cheaper to roll out than changing client code.
Sylvie: But rate-limiting could hurt controllers that expect immediate consistency. We need an approval ticket for safety toggles.
Maria: Config-bot reports active hosts=1,150. Baseline fetch frequency is ~0.08/s per host => baseline qps ~92. If TTL->0 immediate worst-case qps ~=1,150. So delta ~1,058 qps, matches what we saw.
Vik: Client change: fetch-on-invalidate should pick a random backoff between 0 and 2500ms, then exponential backoff on failures. Roll that as a small SDK patch. That plus server-side rate-limit should cut peak by ~60-75%.
Lee: Action plan IMHO: 1) pause change ch-7a2b (done), 2) console block TTL==0 for prod (hotfix), 3) runtime short-coercion hotpatch TTL_min=500ms for 60m (Vik), 4) implement preview preflight estimator API (Maria), 5) telemetry-tagging and dash (Lee), 6) owners outreach + RFC on TTL semantics (Sylvie).
Sylvie: I'll ping owners and open the approval ticket. Also will add the dash tile so oncall can see the delta.
Vik: I'll open the runtime hotpatch PR and the console validation PR. Will aim to ship within 45m and monitor. Need one +1 from platform and SRE.
Maria: I'll wire up a mocked estimator in the preview API so console shows a risk score for changes before publish.
Lee: Please include an ops checklist in the publish flow: run estimator, increase sampling for config_fetch to 100% for the first 10 minutes, confirm owners tagged.
config-bot: Note: change ch-7a2b paused by platform-admin.
Vik: +1 to the plan. Shipping hotpatch now. :thumbsup:
Maria: Thanks all. I'll update the ticket with the action items and we can meet in 30m for status.
